methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-institutional, multinational cohort (Calgary, Würzburg, Heidelberg, Athens, Toulouse) of 21 patients relapsing post-talquetamab with integrated WGS (100x, n=20), scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, targeted sequencing, flow cytometry, AlphaFold2 multimer structural modeling, TCE-binding/cytotoxicity assays, and cell-line functional validation. Analytic pipelines include NYGC variant calling (Mutect2, Strelka2, Lancet), BICSEQ2/CNVkit, ASCAT, FACETS, InferCNV, ArchR, SigProfiler, mmsig, dNdScv, and GISTIC2. Limitations explicitly acknowledged: primary sample experiments performed only once due to limited material. Small cohort limits generalizability but each patient is characterized deeply.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Identifies three convergent antigen-escape mechanisms at GPRC5D in 68.4% of relapsed patients after talquetamab, with direct implications for next-line immunotherapy selection (different TCEs with distinct epitope specificity/affinity/valency differentially target mutant subclones). Findings inform rational use of sequential TCEs in multiple myeloma, a clinically pressing question. Molecular mechanistic cohort study of clinical specimens -> Oxford LoE 4.

reporting_quality.justification: Ethics approvals from five institutions cited, ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers (NCT04108195, NCT04634552) listed, detailed sequencing pipelines and tool versions documented. Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary referenced. Prior published data (GSE199373, GSE199268, GSE199359) explicitly linked. Cell-line and plasmid availability described. Methods are comprehensive and reproducible.

novelty_literature.justification: First comprehensive genomic/transcriptomic/epigenomic characterization of GPRC5D antigen escape after talquetamab, defining three mutational mechanisms including ER-trapping missense mutations in GPCR conserved motifs. Convergent evolution of multiple GPRC5D-mutant subclones within individual patients is a field-defining observation. Demonstrates differential susceptibility to anti-GPRC5D TCEs with different epitope specificities, offering a rational framework for sequencing TCEs. High novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Nature-style manuscript with exemplary integration of multi-modal data. Figures progress from clinical/phylogenetic landscape through each patient's mechanism with complementary flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, and cytotoxicity data. Structural modeling and functional validation are clearly contextualized. Writing is precise and conclusions carefully supported by each data type.

key_strengths: First comprehensive genomic characterization of GPRC5D antigen escape after talquetamab (n=21, 68.4% with escape)
Three convergent mechanisms defined: biallelic deletion, mono+SNV/indel, and epigenetic silencing
Multi-omic integration (WGS, scRNA, scATAC, flow, structural modeling, functional assays)
Differential targeting of mutant subclones by TCEs with different epitopes directly informs therapeutic sequencing
Strong mechanistic insight with AlphaFold2 structural modeling for ER-trapping mutations
key_concerns: Primary CD138+ sample experiments performed only once due to material constraints
Only 8 pre-therapy samples available for paired WGS
Sample acquisition across five institutions introduces technical heterogeneity
Two patients used a reference normal (NA12878) instead of matched normal
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-impact, mechanism-rich study with direct therapeutic implications for multiple myeloma sequencing of T cell engagers; fits top-tier oncology/cancer biology venues (Nature Medicine, Nature Cancer, Cancer Cell).
